newsitem.title: USA: JPE sees moderate loss to breakeven Q4.
newsitem.headline: JPE sees moderate loss to breakeven Q4.

text.p: JPE Inc, reporting a third-quarter loss after taking a goodwill writedown, said it expects the fourth quarter to show a moderate loss or break even.
"Our outlook for the fourth quarter is for a moderate loss to breakeven performance," chairman John Psarouthakis said in a statement.

The truck and automotive components manufacturer also said its board named Psarouthakis to the additional positions of president and chief operating officer. Gareth Reed resigned as president effective October 15.
JPE reported a third-quarter loss of $3.9 million or $0.85 per share compared to a year-ago profit of $880,000 or $0.22 per share. Sales rose to $50.1 million from $44.9 million.

The current quarter has pretax charges, including a $4.3 million writedown of goodwill, $1.4 million in inventory valuation reserves and $450,000 for severance costs. It also includes a $400,000 writedown of an equity investment.

JPE said the downturn in operating performance for the quarer is due to higher scrap, startup costs associated with new product launches and excess costs related to on-time deliveries at its Industrial & Automotive Fasteners and Starboard subsidiaries.
Psarouthakis said the company has made management changes at these two business units.
JPE also said it reviewed the third-quarter charges with its bank group which agreed to amend the company's revolving credit agreement to accommodate the impact of the charges on future quarters.
